findings.title: keychain_has's cached hit ignores keychain_on(), unlike cursor_keychain_has
findings.detail: cursor_keychain_has() checks cursor_keychain_on() before consulting its FOUND cache, so turning the Cursor Keychain copy off makes it return false immediately (line 11437). keychain_has()'s `fresh()` closure, by contrast, only scans the SEEN vec and never calls keychain_on(); keychain_on() is only reached inside the uncached branch via keychain() (line 11238). So if a config_dir's item was seen within the last LOOK_EVERY (2s) and the Keychain copy is then turned off (use_keychain(false, ..), e.g. via a config reload that sets claudeKeychain: false), keychain_has — and therefore has_login/signed_in for that Claude account — keeps reporting the login present for up to 2s even though the copy is now off, unlike the symmetric Cursor path.

findings.title: keychain_has's SEEN cache grows unboundedly for config_dirs no longer queried
findings.detail: The static SEEN Vec only drops a config_dir's entry when keychain_has is called again for that same dir (the retain() call fires on the next lookup, line 11304). An account whose configDir is removed from the config, or one looked up only once, leaves its (PathBuf, Instant) entry in the process-global Vec for the life of the obid process even though it is no longer 'fresh'. Over a long-running obid that adds/removes accounts with distinct configDirs over time this is unbounded, never-reclaimed growth — a slow leak rather than a self-expiring cache.

findings.title: Stale test comment and no coverage of the new throttling behaviour
findings.detail: The comment says Cursor Keychain item presence is checked 'each time' a status is asked (only the token value was throttled to once a minute via cursor_keychain_live). This diff now also caches the presence check itself (cursor_keychain_has) for LOOK_EVERY (2s), so the three back-to-back /v1/status calls in this test perform the underlying 'security find-generic-password' existence probe once instead of three times. The test only asserts on '-w' value-read counts, so it still passes but documents behavior the diff just reverted, and the PR's headline change (status no longer asking security on every call) ships with no assertion that keychain_has/cursor_keychain_has are actually throttled.
